summary: Implemented the provider-neutral, single-subject artwork generation coordination in src/ArrTags/Artwork (docs/architecture.md section 9; docs/data-model.md sections 3.7-3.8; ADR-002/ADR-003/ADR-009/ADR-010). ArtworkGenerationRequest carries the canonical caller inputs (Jellyfin item id, V1 surface, MediaIdentity, MediaMatch, optional BadgeMetadata, ordered BadgeDefinition snapshot, secret-free configuration fingerprint, effective RenderOutputPolicy, OperationalLimits, renderer/badge schema versions) with no source bytes, artifact, provider DTO, path, entity, or credential. ArtworkGenerationCoordinator composes IArtworkSourceReader, IRenderer, and ArtworkPublisher: it observes the current source, builds the SourceImageInput and RenderRequest, calls IRenderer.RenderAsync, and calls ArtworkPublisher.PublishAsync only when the render is Rendered. An absent source is a bounded no-op; a failed source read (item-not-found, unsupported surface/content type, oversized bytes, oversized dimensions, unreadable) preserves the artwork and does not call the renderer or publisher; a render pass-through (including the renderer's existing NoMetadata, MatchNotEligible, IneligibleSurface, NoDisplayableValue, and SourceUnavailable reasons) and a failed render preserve the artwork and never publish. Missing metadata and an ineligible match rely on the existing ADR-009/ADR-010 renderer pass-through convention; no new badge policy was added and no mutation occurs. ArtworkGenerationOutcome and the bounded ArtworkGenerationResult distinguish published, no-source/absent, source-unavailable, render-pass-through, render-failed, publication-not-completed, blocked, and cancelled, carrying only the safe source/render/publication classification and never a secret, path, entity, source bytes, or artifact. Cancellation is honored and no exception escapes; the coordinator never calls Jellyfin directly and the publisher owns all image mutation. For the source-consistency consideration, the exact source observation the coordinator rendered from is supplied to the publisher's new-session capture through a new additive plugin-internal ArtworkPublisher.PublishAsync(request, observedSource, ct) overload, so the retained provenance baseline and the derived artifact describe the same bounded observation; this closes the window in which an independent publisher capture at a later instant could retain a source different from the rendered one. The public publisher overload and its behavior are unchanged, and the before-mutation revalidation is unchanged, so a source that changes after the observation still prevents the mutation. ArrTagsServiceRegistrator registers IRenderer (SkiaBadgeRenderer) and ArtworkGenerationCoordinator with the existing lazy factory pattern and no startup work; no event, queue, library-scan, lifecycle-fencing (5.9), Enhanced coexistence (5.10), route/client (5.11), or caching/invalidation (Phase 6) wiring was added.

known_limitations: The render source is the observed active surface. Selecting the retained original artifact as the render source for a repeat publication while an ArrTags session is already owned (publication-flow step 4, 'render v2 from the retained original artifact') is an explicit boundary of this task: the coordinator reads the current source through IArtworkSourceReader and does not consult PublishedArtworkState/SourceArtifactStore, and the pipeline that selects the retained source belongs to Phase 6. This is documented in docs/architecture.md section 9 and in the coordinator remarks. The publisher still refuses to capture an ArrTags output as a new source when it reuses a retained artifact, and it revalidates ownership before any mutation, so this boundary cannot overwrite an externally changed image.

No event, queue, hosted-lifecycle startup scan, library-event, scheduled, or caching/invalidation wiring was added; ArtworkGenerationCoordinator is an invocable boundary only and Phase 6 drives it. Lifecycle fencing and guarded restoration (5.9), Enhanced coexistence (5.10), and route/client tests (5.11) remain out of scope.

The coordinator reads the current source before the renderer decides metadata eligibility, so a non-matched or metadata-less item still incurs one bounded source read before the renderer passes through. This matches the task's stated flow (read the source, then render); no early eligibility short-circuit was added because it would duplicate renderer policy.

No live-host, native-Skia, or package-content validation was performed for this task: the coordinator test doubles exercise the composition and preservation behavior without a live host, and the task states a guarded live-host test is acceptable but not required. No real Jellyfin library was mutated.

The additive internal ArtworkPublisher.PublishAsync overload accepts a pre-observed source only from plugin-internal callers (the coordinator) and rejects a non-present observation; the public overload is unchanged, so an external caller still cannot inject a source baseline and the task 5.5 ownership guarantees are not weakened.
